description: Break down news coverage volume over time by source language or source country, returning a multi-series time series (one series per language or country). Shows which countries or languages drove early vs. late coverage — useful for tracing how a story propagated geographically or across language communities. Ranks every series by the sum of its values and returns limit of them per page (default 10, cap 75); when more remain it returns nextOffset — pass it back as offset with otherwise identical inputs for the next page. otherSeriesLabels names every series not on the page — pass any labels as the series input to get only those series, complete. Every series carries sum (its ranking key), pointCount, and peak; includePoints: false leaves out its data points for a lighter ranking. GDELT answers a timestep without matching coverage with 0 and leaves out a timestep its own data lacks; missingTimesteps counts those left out between the first and last returned. Each series whose name maps to one GDELT source code carries operator (sourcecountry:<FIPS> or sourcelang:<language>) — add it to a gdelt_search_articles or gdelt_get_coverage_timeline query to read that source's articles or volume. Values are normalized: each point is the topic's share of that source's media output, not an absolute article count, so values from different sources do not add up to a share. Small media markets with concentrated coverage therefore rank above large markets with diverse output — a high value means the topic dominated that source's coverage, not that it published the most articles. Use breakdownBy "country" with the signal-detection chain to map geographic attention, or "language" to detect non-English media surges.

breakdownBy.description: Breakdown dimension: "language" for source language time series, "country" for source country time series.

endDatetime.description: End datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20240131235959). Must pair with startDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected. The window may predate the last 3 months. The window must span at least 30 minutes, the shortest the GDELT DOC API accepts; a shorter one is answered from the server's local GKG mirror where one runs, and refused otherwise.

includePoints.description: Whether each series carries its data points. false returns every series of topSeries or selectedSeries without data, keeping its label, operator, sum, pointCount, and peak; ranking, paging, otherSeriesLabels, and every other field are unchanged. Default true.

limit.description: Maximum series per page (default 10, cap 75). Larger counts clamp with limitClamp; strict deployments reject them.

offset.description: Zero-based series offset — into the ranked overview, or into the series named in series. Pass nextOffset from the preceding response, with otherwise identical inputs, to get the next page.

query.description: Search query using GDELT syntax. Same operators as gdelt_search_articles: phrases, boolean OR, sourcecountry:, sourcelang:, domain:, theme: (GKG theme identifiers come from gdelt_search_themes).

series.description: Exact series labels to return instead of the ranked overview, e.g. ["Portuguese Volume Intensity", "Vietnamese Volume Intensity"]. Take them verbatim from otherSeriesLabels or topSeries[].label in a response, or from the label list an unknown_series error prints — labels, not operators, which go in query. Each one comes back complete under selectedSeries (its points left out only under includePoints: false), in the order requested (every series carrying it, when several do); a label that matches nothing is rejected rather than silently skipped. Omit to get the ranked overview.

smoothing.description: Trailing moving-average width in timesteps (0–30; 0 or 1 leaves values unsmoothed). Width N needs N source steps, omitting leading steps without a full window and potentially shifting peaks later.

startDatetime.description: Start datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20240101000000). Must pair with endDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected. The window may predate the last 3 months. The window must span at least 30 minutes, the shortest the GDELT DOC API accepts; a shorter one is answered from the server's local GKG mirror where one runs, and refused otherwise.

timespan.description: Time window relative to now, a number followed by its unit, minimum "15min"; other examples: "24h", "7d", "1m". Ignored when startDatetime/endDatetime are set. Maximum 3 months.

name: gdelt_get_coverage_breakdown

attempts.description: Each source tried for this call, in order. Present only when the DOC API did not answer with data and the mirror was consulted.

items.description: One source's outcome for this call.

detail.description: Why, when the outcome has a reason: DOC's failure message or the mirror's.

outcome.description: What the source did: answered, empty (answered with no matches), rate_limited, or unavailable; window_too_short when the DOC API was not asked because the window is under the 30 minutes it accepts; or why the mirror could not answer: not_ready (no completed sync), not_compiled (the query or its timespan is in a form the mirror cannot evaluate), outside_coverage (the window lies outside the days it holds), store_error.

breakdownBy.description: Breakdown dimension used for this response.

coverage.description: Present only when the mirror answered less than the requested window. Every count, share, and article in this response comes from answeredStart through answeredEnd; nothing outside it, or in a missing slot, was counted.

answeredEnd.description: End of the window the mirror answered, ISO 8601 UTC.

answeredStart.description: Start of the window the mirror answered, ISO 8601 UTC.

missingSlots.description: 15-minute GKG slots inside the answered window that the mirror holds no data for.

requestedEnd.description: End of the requested window, ISO 8601 UTC.

requestedStart.description: Start of the requested window, ISO 8601 UTC.

dateResolution.description: Temporal resolution of data points — 15min, hour, or day — as GDELT reports it, or else inferred from the spacing of the returned timesteps. Omitted when GDELT reports none and fewer than two distinct timesteps came back.

effectiveQuery.description: Echoed query string for use in follow-up calls.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unknown_series`: A label passed in the series input matches no series in a non-empty breakdown. `offset_out_of_range`: The requested offset is at or beyond the last series of a non-empty overview, or of the series named in series. `invalid_date_range`: Only one of startDatetime / endDatetime was supplied, one of them is not a real UTC calendar timestamp, startDatetime is not earlier than endDatetime, or the window spans under the 30 minutes the GDELT DOC API accepts and no local GKG mirror answers it in DOC's place. `invalid_query`: GDELT rejected the query string as malformed — bad keyword length, unbalanced parentheses, or an illegal character. `gdelt_rate_limited`: GDELT rejected the request for its one-request-per-five-seconds limit, or too many requests were already queued for this one to start in time. `gdelt_unavailable`: GDELT DOC API is unreachable or temporarily returned no usable data. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

limitClamp.description: Present only when the requested count exceeded the per-call cap: the call ran exactly as a call at the cap, and every count, notice, and continuation in this response reflects the applied value.

applied.description: The per-call cap the call ran with instead.

parameter.description: The count input that was clamped.

requested.description: The value the call asked for.

missingTimesteps.description: Timesteps GDELT left out between the first and last timestep of the whole breakdown, across every series, at dateResolution — gaps in GDELT's data, not zero coverage, which GDELT returns as 0. The notice names each missing run. The same on every page, under series, and with or without points. Omitted when none are missing, and never reported for an answer from the local GKG mirror.

nextOffset.description: Offset of the next page, for the same inputs. Absent when this page reaches the last series.

notice.description: Guidance when the query matched no coverage in the window — how to broaden the query or extend the window — or, when this response is one page of several, which series it returned out of how many. Which timesteps GDELT left out of the breakdown (see missingTimesteps), and what smoothing omits. When the server's local GKG mirror answered (source: gkg_mirror), why, how its figures differ from the DOC API's, and how many matching articles a country breakdown left out for having no known source country. Absent when the DOC API answered a complete, unsmoothed breakdown whose every series fit in one response.

otherSeriesLabels.description: Label of every ranked series not on this page, in rank order, on every overview page. Pass any of them to the series input to retrieve that series' complete data. Omitted when this page holds every series, or when the series input selects series instead.

selectedSeries.description: Complete, untruncated time series for the labels requested via the series input — those of this page, in the order requested, without their points under includePoints: false. Omitted when series was not supplied.

items.description: A single language or country coverage series.

data.description: Time-ordered data points for this series. Present when includePoints is true (the default); omitted when it is false.

items.description: A single data point for this series.

value.description: Normalized coverage volume at this timestep — the topic's share of this source's media output, not an absolute article count.

label.description: Series label (language name or country name).

operator.description: Paste-ready DOC query operator for this series' source: sourcecountry:<FIPS code> for a country (FIPS, not ISO — AU is Austria) or sourcelang:<language name> for a language. Add it to a gdelt_search_articles or gdelt_get_coverage_timeline query to see that source's articles or volume. Omitted when the series name maps to no GDELT code or to more than one.

peak.description: The point of the whole series with the largest absolute value, the earliest on a tie. Omitted when the series has no points.

date.description: Timestep of the peak, in ISO 8601 format.

pointCount.description: Data points GDELT returned for the whole series — fewer than the timesteps in the window when GDELT left some out (see missingTimesteps).

sum.description: Sum of the series' values over every point GDELT returned for it — the key the overview ranks series by. It ranks series and is neither a share of anything nor an article count.

source.description: Where this answer came from: doc_api, the GDELT DOC API, or gkg_mirror, the server's local mirror of GDELT's Global Knowledge Graph, which answers when the DOC API refuses the request or returns nothing, and in its place when the startDatetime/endDatetime window is under the 30 minutes the DOC API accepts. Present on every answer while the server runs a mirror; absent otherwise.

staleResponse.description: Present only when the refetch of this exact request was refused, failed, or came back empty, and the response is GDELT's stored answer from fetchedAt instead. It holds nothing published after fetchedAt; a relative timespan covers the window ending at fetchedAt, not now. Absent on a live answer.

ageSeconds.description: Age of the stored answer when served, in whole seconds.

fetchedAt.description: ISO 8601 time GDELT returned the stored answer.

reason.description: Why the refetch was not used: GDELT rate-limited it, did not answer with data, or answered empty — which GDELT also does under load.

topSeries.description: The ranked overview: every series ranked by the sum of its values, those of this page in rank order, each with its points unless includePoints is false. Omitted when the series input selects series instead.

items.description: A single language or country coverage series.

data.description: Time-ordered data points for this series. Present when includePoints is true (the default); omitted when it is false.

items.description: A single data point for this series.

value.description: Normalized coverage volume at this timestep — the topic's share of this source's media output, not an absolute article count.

label.description: Series label (language name or country name).

operator.description: Paste-ready DOC query operator for this series' source: sourcecountry:<FIPS code> for a country (FIPS, not ISO — AU is Austria) or sourcelang:<language name> for a language. Add it to a gdelt_search_articles or gdelt_get_coverage_timeline query to see that source's articles or volume. Omitted when the series name maps to no GDELT code or to more than one.

peak.description: The point of the whole series with the largest absolute value, the earliest on a tie. Omitted when the series has no points.

date.description: Timestep of the peak, in ISO 8601 format.

pointCount.description: Data points GDELT returned for the whole series — fewer than the timesteps in the window when GDELT left some out (see missingTimesteps).

sum.description: Sum of the series' values over every point GDELT returned for it — the key the overview ranks series by. It ranks series and is neither a share of anything nor an article count.

totalCount.description: Total number of series GDELT returned, before paging.
